messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists
function.description: Retrieves a list of all artists whose works are present in a museum during a particular period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

period.description: The time period for which to retrieve the artists, e.g., 19th Century.

country.description: The country where the museum is located, optional parameter. Default: 'USA'

message.content:
**Famous 19th‑Century Dancers (and Dance Innovators)**  

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions / Roles |
|------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1815‑1897) | Swedish | The “Queen of the Romantic Ballet”; famed for her ethereal pointe technique and the iconic “La Sylphide.” |
| **Carlotta Grisi** (1819‑1893) | Italian | Star of “Giselle” and “La Sylphide”; known for her lyrical style and expressive phrasing. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810‑1884) | Austrian | One of the era’s most celebrated virtuoso ballerinas; her dramatic flair and technical brilliance set new standards. |
| **Jules Perrot** (1793‑1875) | French | Choreographer and dancer who shaped the Paris Opera Ballet; created works such as “La Fille mal gardée.” |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818‑1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of the Imperial Russian Ballet; laid the groundwork for the “Golden Age” of ballet with ballets like *Swan Lake* (though premiered 1877). |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850‑1928) | Italian | Renowned teacher and choreographer; developed the Cecchetti method, a foundational ballet technique still taught worldwide. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1805‑1865) | Italian | Dance theorist and pedagogue; authored *Principles of the Art of Dancing*, influencing ballet training across Europe. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1888‑1931) | Russian | Though her career peaked in the early 20th century, she was born in the 19th century and became one of the most iconic ballerinas of the era. |
| **John Neumeier** (born 1942) | German | While primarily a 20th‑century choreographer, his early work in the 1970s was heavily influenced by 19th‑century Romantic ballet traditions. |
| **George Balanchine** (1904‑1983) | Russian‑American | Born in the early 20th century, he was deeply inspired by 19th‑century ballet and helped modernize it; his legacy reflects the Romantic era’s influence. |

> **Note:** This list highlights some of the most influential dancers, choreographers, and teachers whose work defined or was shaped by the 19th‑century ballet world. It is by no means exhaustive—many other performers contributed to the rich tapestry of dance during this period.
